$comment: Who owns each committed data file, in a form a program can read.
Prose said this in four places and none of them was checked, so a file
could be hand-edited, or written by a pipeline and never committed, and
nothing noticed. tests/test_generated_files.py holds this table to the
repository: every path here exists, every writer here exists, and every
committed data file is classified by it.
`staged_by_refresh` is the list scripts/refresh-daily.sh commits. It is
read from this file rather than retyped into a workflow, which is how
data/drought/usdm-huc4.json came to be recomputed every morning and
`appears_when` marks a path whose writer creates it only under a stated
condition, so it is owned and classified from the day the writer learns
to write it rather than from the day it first appears. Everything else
in this table still has to exist.

classes.generated-daily: Rewritten by the scheduled refresh. Never hand-edit; change the writer and run it.
classes.generated-weekly: Downloaded by the scheduled refresh when the producer publishes. Never hand-edit.
classes.generated-archive: Append-only history written by a generator. Never hand-edit, never rewrite in place.
classes.derived-on-demand: Rebuilt by a named tool when its inputs change, not by the daily job.
classes.reviewed-by-hand: Edited by a person, carrying the evidence for each entry.
classes.frozen: Retained for compatibility and parity checks. Do not regenerate.

files.note: The published reservoir payload. This commit is the deploy (ADR-002).

One frozen file per finished water year, snowpack-wy<YEAR>.json: snowpack.json byte for byte as published on the season's last morning, copied by the first refresh of the next water year before it overwrites the payload (ADR-121). Write-once; never rewritten. A directory entry, so the season that ends next year is classified and committed without editing this table.
Accumulated precipitation since 1 October at the snow stations (ADR-125). Separate from snowpack.json so a failure costs only this file.
The last fifteen days of soil moisture at the snow stations and each station's seven-day change (ADR-142). Separate from snowpack.json and precipitation.json so a failure costs only this file.

Every day the daily river refresh has read, per gauge: flow, review status, qualifiers and, at a natural gauge, the flow class (ADR-146). Merged by date, so a revised value replaces that day. Nothing is deleted. No page fetches it yet.
For each refresh date, the week's change published for each drainage area, with the stations behind it (ADR-146). Starts on the first run; no earlier day is rebuilt. No page fetches it yet.

files.appears_when: the first daily refresh after refresh_lakes.py lands writes it from admitted_terminal_lakes.json
files.note: The natural terminal lakes payload (ADR-112): elevation and volume, no capacity or percent full. Separate from reservoirs.json on purpose; a lake joins no reservoir rollup.

The daily surface level of each reservoir on admitted_reservoir_elevations.json, from the provider's first reading (ADR-135). Fetched only by those reservoirs' pages; reservoirs.json carries the summary and never the series.
Verified exclusive polygons. Reverted rather than published alone when coverage fails.

The week usdm-current.geojson replaced, kept so a change between two weeks can be measured from the polygons rather than from basin shares. Rotated only when the map date actually moves. No page fetches it and the build does not publish it.
files.appears_when: the monitor publishes a week after the one held in usdm-current.geojson

files.note: The default level. Must describe the same week as the polygons.
The other offered level (ADR-064). A reader who changes the level fetches this file, so it is committed with the others or it strands them on another week.

The coarsest offered level (ADR-073). Committed with the other two for the same reason: a reader who changes the level fetches this file, and a week behind the others is a level that disagrees with itself.
The drought-only subbasin level (ADR-088). It is committed with the other coverage files but starts without an archive or previous-week claim.

One archive per level; merge_history refuses a payload at another. This is where the default level's previous week comes from. A decade of weeks, each measured from the monitor's archived map; tools/backfill_drought_history.py --rebuild measured the weeks before the weekly run (ADR-122).
The subregion archive (ADR-074). Its weeks before the weekly run were measured from the monitor's archived maps, like the basin one (ADR-122).
The region archive, on the same terms as the subregion one.
Derived from capacities, counties and the boundary files. tests/test_refresh.py runs the same --check comparison, so drift fails the build.
A median over a period that has ended cannot change. Network job; every run merges.

Daily mean river flow at the reviewed gauges in admitted_river_gauges.json (ADR-136): 30 days per gauge with approval status and qualifiers. A natural gauge's newest value carries its day-of-year percentile band and class from river_normals.json (ADR-144); a shaped gauge has no normal. No rank and no total across gauges.

Day-of-year flow percentiles (10th to 90th) for the natural river gauges, read from the U.S. Geological Survey's statistics service (ADR-144). The daily refresh reads it and never fetches it. Moves when the survey approves another year of values; network job; every run merges. Never copied to dist.
Every water year from 1991 at each snow station whose record covers all of them (ADR-125). Rebuilt each October after the year closes; network job; every run merges.
What drains to each published reservoir, traced once against NLDI and committed with its COMID evidence (ADR-077). Rebuild when the roster or snow network changes; published verbatim in dist.

A committed reference, read once from the legacy USGS WaterServices daily values (shut down 2027-02-22) and never refreshed: the mean discharge of each complete water year at Duchesne River near Randlett (09302000), with source URL, fetched_at, parameter and approval-code counts. tools/build_gauge_review.py reads it for the years the OGC v1 daily series lacks. Its writer cannot run once the legacy service ends; the file is the record.

Proposed operating characters (ADR-114) and natural-lake flags for every published reservoir, with the inventory and hydrography evidence behind each. Candidates for a reviewer: nothing here is applied to a roster or a payload, and no page fetches it. Rebuild when the roster changes or a service is asked again.

One run of the New Mexico admission screen (R11): every storage series the state has on USGS, RISE and the Corps' Albuquerque District, matched to its dam, with the drawn-scope check and a suggestion. Candidates for a reviewer: nothing here is applied to a roster or a payload, and no page fetches it.
A missing mask stops the drought run rather than reporting border basins as drought-free (ADR-059).
The drawn scope. Committed for reproducible analysis, never copied to dist/.
The ten-basin research scope. Registered, not published.
Reviewed Conservation Service admissions.
Reviewed Reclamation admissions.
Reviewed California admissions, plus the withheld block naming every candidate kept out and the finding behind it. A waiver with no reason is refused by the loader.
Reviewed Colorado admissions, plus the withheld block naming every candidate kept out and the finding behind it. Keyed by the provider's telemetry abbrev.
Reviewed U.S. Geological Survey admissions (ADR-098).
Reviewed Salt River Project admissions and pinned measurement identities.
Reviewed Montana DNRC admission and explicit no-NID finding (ADR-099).
Reviewed U.S. Army Corps of Engineers admissions for the Columbia Basin (ADR-102), with the withheld block naming every location kept out and why.
Reviewed Central Arizona Project admission of Lake Pleasant, with the reviewed full-level finding (ADR-104).

The reviewed river gauges (ADR-136): display and survey names, the primary daily mean series, the tier with its basis and who directed it, and the evidence for any water named downstream. The loader refuses an entry without them.

The reviewed natural terminal lakes (ADR-112): a waterbody point, a closed-basin assignment and two measured series with the volume's relation named. No capacity is recorded for any lake; the loader refuses one.

The reviewed reservoir surface elevations (ADR-135): the provider's elevation item, the vertical datum with its evidence and checked date, the measured offset to the other datum with its measurement date, and reference levels with their authority. The loader refuses an entry missing any of them.
One daily representative per date for dense short-history providers, used to request only missing intervals.
Versioned, size-budgeted reservoir facts for the public question service.
Current snow facts and upstream joins without complete daily series.
Current HUC2/4/6/8 drought facts and the newest 26 weeks of the HUC2/4/6 archives (DROUGHT_HISTORY_WEEKS).
Names only, for the shared header's Find a place search: each reservoir and its state, each drawn drainage area at every level, and each current snow site.
The fourteen-area Utah-connected historical scope, kept for compatibility and parity checks.
Retired as a published mask by ADR-067; retained for parity.

Test fixture: snowpack.json byte for byte as committed at 7791ce7 (as of 2026-09-30), the last full day of water year 2026. The season-shaped unit tests read it because the daily file restarts at one snowless day each 1 October. Never published.

Test fixture: snowpack.json byte for byte as committed at ed71e7b (as of 2026-10-18), seventeen days into water year 2027. Pins what the page does before the season has a peak or a normal worth dividing by (ADR-121). Never published.
